transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC; Duration: 48m; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Ortega (Seabreeze CTO), Marcus Hale (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infra)
Shared artifacts: deck: https://redwood.example/optimize-playbook (shared), cost-sim template (link in chat)

00:00 Maya: Okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll run ~45 minutes, want to make sure we scope a POC around sessionization and KV/prefix caching for your conversational agents. Lina, quick context on goals?
00:18 Lina: Yeah thanks. We're rolling out a SaaS analytics assistant embedded in our product - real time q&a and follow-up. Main concerns are latency under 300ms p50, keeping token cost predictable, and meeting SOC2 for logs. We currently run a homemade on-prem infra but evaluating hosted or dedicated.
00:38 Marcus: our traffic is bursty, peak concurrency hits ~1.2k concurrent sessions, average request length 60 tokens, but follow-up messages reuse context a lot. We think session affinity + KV cache could cut costs.
00:55 Ravi: cool, that's the exact pattern Redwood Optimize targets. Quick clarifying q, are you ok with shared-hosted or you need VPC/private?
01:12 Lina: Ideally VPC for prod, but for POC hosted is fine as long as we can sign an NDA and we don't ship PII.
01:22 Maya: noted. We'll treat POC data as synthetic. Quick agenda: show how prefix/KV caching works, run a cost sim with your session shape, and outline bench.

03:05 Ravi: (screen) Walk-through the console Optimize tab - here's the batching slider, cache TTL, and sessionization knob. The idea: keep per-session KV cache warm so follow-ups read from KV rather than re-tokenizing prefix. This reduces decode tokens per request.
03:45 Marcus: when you say KV cache, is that per-session in memory on the GPU or persisted?
03:50 Ravi: good q, by default KV is per-inference node memory (persisted across short-lived requests) - we call it prefix cache; for Dedicated you can pin sessions to a pool and keep it longer. There's also an optional Redis-backed cold store for longer session slots but that adds retrieval latency.
04:12 Priya: is retrieval over network crypto-ed? we need encryption at rest/in transit and KMS support.
04:18 Maya: yes, encryption in transit, and for Private we plug into your KMS/HSM. We'll share the KMS integration notes in the security pack.

06:00 Ravi: demo scenario: baseline no-cache p50 latency 270ms decode heavy; with prefix cache warmed we see decode down 45% and cost per convo down ~38% in this sim. Note: tradeoff is increased memory use and slightly higher tail latency on cache-miss.
06:30 Marcus: can you quantify tail latency impact? we care p95 < 900ms.
06:35 Ravi: on sample runs p95 grew from 520ms to 660ms for the warmed config; on cold-starts p95 can spike above 1s but with session affinity and prefetch you avoid most of those.

08:50 Maya: quick qualification - what's your SLA must-have and decision timeline?
09:00 Lina: we need production SLA discussions by end of Q3, POC by mid-June. If cost and latency meet targets we'll look Dedicated for prod.
09:12 Maya: perfect that's doable.

10:40 Marcus: about batching: our bursts are short ~30s and then idle; how does continuous batching interact?
10:55 Ravi: Redwood's runtime does adaptive batching: it collects micro-batches on the node up to latency budget. For short bursts it's advantageous to use dynamic batching with a strict latency threshold; for your type we recommend conservative batch sizes (2-4) and aggressive prefix cache to keep tokens low.
11:25 Priya: what about concurrency limits? our cluster can't allocate thousands of GPUs.
11:32 Ravi: for Hosted we autoscale; for Dedicated you reserve GPU pools. There's a cost trade-off: reserve more to keep high concurrency and low queueing; otherwise requests queue and increase latency. We'll simulate both in the cost model.

14:00 (Ravi shares cost-sim spreadsheet)
14:18 Ravi: here's the cost model: inputs are qps, avg tokens, follow-up ratio, session stickiness. We can toggle quantization profile (int8 vs int4) and routing to lower-cost model variants for fallback.
14:45 Marcus: can Redwood route to a smaller quantized model for low-priority requests to save $$?
14:50 Ravi: yes, smart routing policy can send background/analytics queries to cheaper model, while live user-facing traffic hits higher perf variant. That reduces unit cost but adds routing complexity.

17:30 Lina: security checklist - SOC 2, audit logs, RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta). Do you have SOC2 cert?
17:40 Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll attach the cert. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available via Console. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported.
17:55 Marcus: for data residency we may need EU-only. Does Hosted support region pinning?
18:02 Maya: yes we can pin region and for Private we'll deploy in your VPC.

20:10 Priya: curious about KV eviction policies - LRU? TTL?
20:15 Ravi: default is LRU + TTL; you can set session TTL by time or by token budget. For sessions with longer context, you can prefetch KV on session resume to reduce cold misses.

22:00 Marcus: show a concrete example with our numbers please.
22:05 Ravi: sure - import your sample heatmap (you sent earlier), set avg seq=60, follow-up rate 0.7, session stickiness 0.6, bursts peaking at 1.2k. With prefix cache + small-batching our sim shows cost down 34% and p50 220ms; without cache cost is materially higher.
22:40 Lina: that's promising. Any hidden costs: cache memory, infra?
22:45 Ravi: memory on Dedicated is part of node sizing; for Hosted it's absorbed but visible on the bill as memory-backed nodes. We'll break this out in the sim. Also mention of increased stateful node counts in Dedicated raises committed cost.

25:10 (short crosstalk)
25:25 Marcus: latency variability: if a cache miss hits during a burst does the scheduler deprioritize?
25:30 Ravi: the scheduler doesn't deprioritize but we have fast fallbacks: if KV miss and queue depth makes latency unacceptable, route to a lower-latency model variant or a smaller sequence short-circuit. Fallback rules are configurable.

28:45 Priya: about bench: for the POC we'd want a synthetic replay at your infra that mimics our session churn and 95/99 tail reporting.
28:55 Maya: yes we'll run bench with your heatmap; propose 2-hour long highlights with progressive ramp to peak, capture p50/p95/p99 and token-cost per minute.
29:10 Marcus: do you need access to our environment?
29:15 Maya: for Private/Dedicated bench maybe; for hosted we can run synthetic traffic against a test model. For on-prem we'd do an agent install.

31:40 Lina: a few risk items internally: legal needs data retention controls and ability to purge sessions. Is that possible?
31:48 Maya: yes retention policies and purge APIs exist — we'll include purge examples in the security pack.

33:20 Ravi: demonstration of prefetch policy: we can prefetch KV for active sessions predicted to send a follow-up. Prediction window can be tuned so prefetch doesn't waste memory.
33:40 Marcus: how accurate is the follow-up predictor? false positives could waste cache memory.
33:45 Ravi: typical predictor precision in our customers is ~0.78 on similar chat workloads; you can set confidence thresholds to balance memory vs hit-rate. We'll run A/B tests during POC.

36:05 Priya: network egress costs — if we keep KV warm across regions does that incur cross-region traffic?
36:12 Ravi: yes cross-region prefetching is discouraged; normal deployment pins sessions to region to avoid egress. For Dedicated in multi-region you can replicate state but that adds cost. We'll model region egress in the sim.

39:20 Maya: recap: POC scope — 2-week bench with hosted synthetic first, then Dedicated trial if numbers look good. Deliverables: cost sim, security pack, bench schedule.
39:40 Lina: agreed, please also include a minimal SLO draft for p50/p95/p99 for our legal review.
39:48 Maya: will do.

41:00 (quick objection) Marcus: we've budgeted for something like 25% cost reduction. If POC shows 10% we probably won't switch. Can you guarantee numbers?
41:12 Ravi: can't guarantee but the sim uses your heatmap; we'll surface assumptions and confidence intervals. Also we can run a controlled A/B in prod pilot to measure real impact.
41:30 Lina: ok.

43:00 Maya: next steps in chat: I'll drop the security pack and SSO docs now; Ravi will upload cost sim and a few scenario toggles; Marcus/Priya to confirm bench window, Lina to loop in Legal/Security.

46:10 Priya: final q - do you support model quantization on the fly?
46:18 Ravi: yes we have quantization profiles; changing profile requires model variant deployment but runtime can route traffic between variants. We recommend simming int8 then int4 to watch quality regressions.

47:05 Maya: great thanks everyone. I'll follow up with notes and next steps.
47:12 Lina: thanks all.

End of meeting.
